events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 14:14:50 and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged [F4][F8]. Because the cancellation was made by the driver on a no-show claim, NS-0 routes the case through NS-1/NS-2 [F4][RD-1 not applicable here; NS-0]. NS-1 requires all three of (i) an "I'm Here" tap / platform arrival confirmation, (ii) GPS placement within the pickup range at the moment of the tap, and (iii) waiting at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes. Element (iii) is measured by the system records, which override the driver's chat and statement [F11][F12][NS-1].

The GPS and timeline records show the driver first came within 200 m of the pickup at 14:12:20 and accumulated only 2 min 30 s inside that radius before cancelling at 14:14:50 [F2][F4][F5]; the platform timeline itself records arrival at 14:12:20 and cancellation 2 min 30 s later [F5][F4]. Counting from his own "I'm Here" tap at 14:13:10, he remained in range for only 1 min 40 s before cancelling [F6][F4]. On either reading the >3-minute requirement of NS-1(iii) is not satisfied.

The driver's contemporaneous chat claim of waiting "more than 3 min" [F11] and his written statement to the same effect [F12] conflict with the GPS and timeline records [F2][F5], and under the system-record rule the records prevail, so NS-1(iii) fails. As NS-1 is not fully satisfied, the exception in NS-2 applies and the $6.61 fee cannot stand. The refund amount is the cancellation fee carried on the fare record, $6.61, with no surge multiplier (1.0×) to adjust it [F8][F9][NS-2]. It issues as an in-app voucher rather than cash, and Ryde retains final discretion [NS-7].

No account flag is warranted: the "I'm Here" tap was made 39 m from the pickup point (closest approach 38 m) [F6][F1], so the NS-2 aggravated limb (tapping while not at the pickup point) is not triggered, and the driver's 90-day record shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld [F17][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as an in-app Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag against the driver.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled as a passenger no-show but the GPS record shows he was inside the 200 m pickup zone for a cumulative 2 min 30 s only — 14:12:20 to cancellation at 14:14:50 — which is below the >3 minutes required for a cancellation fee to stand.

The timeline records the driver tapping "I'm Here" at 14:13:10, so only 1 min 40 s of in-zone waiting elapsed between his own arrival button and his cancellation at 14:14:50, again short of the >3 minute threshold.

The driver's chat message "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (14:14) and his written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited" are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records of 2 min 30 s total in-zone time; the system records win, so NS-1(iii) fails.
Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee of record must be refunded to the rider in full under NS-2.
The refund is $6.61, the exact cancellation fee carried on the fare record, and no surge applied (multiplier 1.0×) so no reduction or uplift is warranted.

weaknesses: The driver did reach the pickup area and waited: F1 (closest approach 38 m) and F3 (stationary 2 min 0 s at 41 m from pickup) show he was genuinely present, so the rider's absence is not disputed — only the duration threshold saves the rider.

F6 shows he did tap "I'm Here" at 14:13:10 while 39 m away, satisfying NS-1(i) and (ii); the other side will argue the 3-minute wait should run from platform-recorded arrival at 14:12:20 (F5), which is only 10 seconds short of the cumulative 2 min 30 s in F2 — the margin is thin and depends on the records being read cumulatively.
F11/F12 show the driver's contemporaneous claim of waiting more than 3 minutes; the judge must prefer the GPS/timeline records (F2, F5) over these statements.
The rider's own profile (F16) shows 1 prior dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld, offering no supporting pattern for this complaint.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: his closest approach was 38 m and he remained within 200 m of the pickup from 14:12:20 until cancellation, satisfying the 'at the pick-up location' element of NS-1 (ii).

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10 while 39 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 1 min 40 s afterwards, satisfying NS-1 (i) and keeping him inside the pickup range at the moment of the tap.

The driver's stationary period at 41 m from the pickup ran 14:12:50–14:14:50 (2 min 0 s stationary within 200 m counting from 14:12:20 he accumulated only 2 min 30 s inside the 200 m radius before cancelling), so the NS-1 (iii) requirement of more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) is not met and the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand.

The platform's own timeline records the driver as having arrived at 14:12:20 and cancelling 2 min 30 s later, which is under the 3-minute threshold, so under NS-2 the cancellation fee of $6.61 must be refunded in full.

The driver's chat message at 14:14 claiming 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' (adopted in his written statement) is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing only 2 min 30 s inside the pickup radius, and system records prevail over statements; treating his self-report as unreliable is the honest reading of the evidence.

Because the driver did press 'I'm Here' while GPS placed him within the pickup range, the NS-2 aggravated limb (fee refund plus flag_account for pressing the button while not at the pickup point) is not triggered — the button was pressed 39 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the range.

Driver presses 'I'm Here' only once and no duplicate or abusive waiting-fee pattern appears in the records, and his 90-day history shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld, so no account flag is warranted against him.

weaknesses: The timeline is internally inconsistent: F6 records a tap of 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10, but F7 states the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null). If the rider relies on F7, at least one NS-1 element (i) fails, which still favours us on the fee but also removes the basis for characterising the tap as legitimate.

The driver's own chat message F11 and statement F12 assert he waited 'more than 3 min'; F2/F3/F5 show only 2 min 30 s inside 200 m and 2 min 0 s stationary, so the rider will use F11/F12 to paint the driver as misreporting his waiting time, and NS-1 (iii) is the exact element that fails.

The driver cancelled 5 min 50 s after acceptance (F4) while the rider had already been matched; the rider will argue she was still en route and that the fee was charged without any valid no-show, which, although consistent with our NS-2 position, invites an account-level look at the cancellation (NS-3).
No traffic or weather factor excuses anything here (F13, F14, F15), so the driver has no external justification narrative if the judge views the 2 min 30 s as borderline.

points.response: Conceded as a factual matter on presence only: F1 (38 m closest approach) and F3 (stationary at 41 m) show the driver was inside the pickup zone, but NS-1(ii) is only one of three cumulative requirements and it cannot carry the fee on its own.

Conceded that NS-1(i) is met on the timeline record (F6, tap at 14:13:10, 39 m from pickup), but that same fact is what fixes the relevant clock: only 1 min 40 s of in-zone time elapsed between that tap and the 14:14:50 cancellation (F4).

Agreed, and I adopt this point: the system records show 2 min 30 s cumulative inside 200 m (F2) and 2 min 0 s stationary (F3) before cancellation at 14:14:50 (F4), so the NS-1(iii) requirement of more than 3 minutes fails and the fee cannot stand.
Adopted: with NS-1(iii) unsatisfied, NS-2 requires a full refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee of record (F8), so the parties in fact converge on refund_full.

Adopted on the outcome: F11 and F12 assert a wait of 'more than 3 min', but F2, F3 and F5 record only 2 min 30 s in zone, and the system records prevail, so the driver's timekeeping is unreliable — though this unreliability is his own admission, not a fraud finding.

Conceded: F6 places the 'I'm Here' tap 39 m from the pickup point and F1 confirms his closest approach was 38 m, so the NS-2 aggravated limb (button pressed outside the pickup range) is not made out and I do not seek a flag against the driver.

Conceded: no duplicate-tap or waiting-fee abuse pattern appears in F6 and the driver's 90-day record (F17) shows 0 upheld disputes, so no flag_account is warranted; the rider's claim is limited to the $6.61 refund.

I do not withdraw C1 and C2: the opposing brief's own D3/D4 accept that only 2 min 30 s (F2) accrued inside the zone, so the finding remains that the $6.61 no-show fee fails NS-1(iii) and is refunded under NS-2; the internal conflict it flags between F6 (tap at 14:13:10) and F7 (driver_pressed_here_at null) is immaterial to my client because either way the fee falls — if F7 governs, NS-1(i) fails outright under NS-2, and if F6 governs, the wait is 1 min 40 s, still under 3 minutes.

Conceded as to the arithmetic — my client was inside the 200 m zone for only 2 min 30 s (F2) from the platform-recorded arrival at 14:12:20 (F5), so NS-1(iii)'s requirement of more than 3 minutes is not met and the fee cannot stand; my brief seeks the same full refund, so this point is not in dispute between the parties.

The rider's own chronology cuts against her: the 'I'm Here' tap at 14:13:10 while 39 m from the pickup point (F6) establishes NS-1(i) and (ii), and it is precisely because only 1 min 40 s of in-zone time followed the tap that NS-2 refund_full — not the aggravated flag_account limb — applies; the driver pressed the button while genuinely within range (F1), so no button-abuse flag is warranted.

Agreed that system records prevail: F2 and F5 show 2 min 30 s of in-zone time, so the driver's F11/F12 statements are unreliable; I do not ask the judge to credit them, and my client accepts the refund rather than defend the 3-minute claim.
No opposition: because NS-1(iii) fails, NS-2 requires refund_full of the $6.61 cancellation fee, which is exactly the outcome my brief requests (F8).
The amount is correct: $6.61 with no surge multiplier (F8, F9), and NS-7 means it issues as an in-app voucher rather than cash — that is the only adjustment I ask the judge to record.
